images.filename: Sea stacks at Porth Wen - geograph.org.uk - 1100666.jpg
images.caption: Sea stacks at Porth Wen These stacks are the remnants of collapsed natural arches. The white mass in the foreground right has a surviving natural arch. Caves can be seen in the Torllwyn headland beyond the stacks. In time these may join with caves on the opposite side of the headland to form natural arches which would eventually collapse to form sea stacks.
images.alt: Sea stacks at Porth Wen These stacks are the remnants of collapsed natural arches. The white mass in the foreground right has a surviving natural arch. Caves can be seen in the Torllwyn headland beyond the stacks. In time these may join with caves on the opposite side of the headland to form natural arches which would eventually collapse to form sea stacks.

images.filename: Silica bunkers at Porth Wen Brick Works - geograph.org.uk - 1104879.jpg
images.caption: Silica bunkers at Porth Wen Brick Works Rock arriving down the incline from the Graig Wen Quarry arrived at the top of the structure - the steel "knapper" used to crush the rock can be seen at the top most level. Pieces of rock then descended down shutes through the various levels where they were further processed - reaching the lower bunkers in almost powder form ready for brick making.
images.alt: Silica bunkers at Porth Wen Brick Works Rock arriving down the incline from the Graig Wen Quarry arrived at the top of the structure - the steel "knapper" used to crush the rock can be seen at the top most level. Pieces of rock then descended down shutes through the various levels where they were further processed - reaching the lower bunkers in almost powder form ready for brick making.
